nodes.name: CeO2 Ionomer Dispersion
nodes.procedure: An aqueous dispersion of CeO₂ containing solution was prepared by adding as-received CeO₂ (6.75 mg, Wako Pure Chemical) to ultrapure water (Millipore Milli-Q) and then ultrasonically dispersing the mixture for 2 h. The anion exchange ionomer solution (AS-4, Tokuyama Corp., diluted to 1 wt% solution with ethanol, 0.7 mL) was then added to the resultant dispersion liquid (0.75 mL) and ultrasonically dispersed for 1 h to obtain the CeO₂ containing ionomer solution.

nodes.name: Pt/Si Electroless Deposition
nodes.procedure: First, to fabricate a Pt nanofilm (~50 nm), the base plane of the Si prism was subjected to hydrophilic treatment with 40% NH₄F solution for 1 min. Palladium was then deposited with 1% HF-1 mM PdCl₂ for 5 min at room temperature. After rinsing, platinum deposition was performed by immersion in Pt plating solution at 50°C for 12 min. Pt plating solution prepared by mixing ELECTROLESS Pt 100 basic solution (30 mL), reducing solution (0.6 mL), 28% NH₃ solution, and ultrapure water.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2 particles have a mean particle diameter of ca. 0.3 μm on the CeO2-modified Pt/Si prism surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As is evident in Figure 3d, the CeO2 particles used in this study had a mean particle diameter of ca. 0.3μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: CVs show hydrogen desorption (0.05-0.45 V), double-layer capacitance (0.45-0.70 V), OH adsorption pseudocapacitance (0.70-0.85 V), and oxide formation (>0.85 V) for both ionomer-coated Pt and CeO2-modified Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2 shows CVs of the disk electrodes in 1M KOH at 25°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: In blank KOH, ionomer-coated Pt shows Pt-OHad librational mode at 1130 cm⁻¹ above 0.7 V; CeO2-modified Pt shows linear potential dependence of Pt-OHad band area independent of CV response.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the case of the CeO2-modified Pt/Si prism, however, the tendency was substantially different. As shown in Figure 7b, the Pt-OHad band area was independent of the CV response but simply responded linearly to the applied potential.

properties.description: Multiple potential-dependent IR spectra showing adsorption features

nodes.characterization_summary: During ammonia oxidation reaction in 1 M KOH-0.1 M NH3, CeO2-modified Pt shows accelerated NOad formation (band at 1504 cm⁻¹, >3x greater) and enhanced N2H4,ad (1269 cm⁻¹), Pt-OHad plateau 0.3-0.9 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the case of the CeO2-modified Pt surface, the same number of bands was observed... the band intensity observed at ca. 1504 cm⁻¹, which originates from the bridged NOad.

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA calculated from H adsorption/desorption region (0.05-0.45 V vs RHE); CeO2-modified Pt/Si = 17.26 cm², ionomer-coated Pt/Si = 11.75 cm² (ratio 1.47).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ratio of ECSA for CeO2-modified Pt/Si to ionomer-coated Pt/Si was 17.26 cm²/11.75 cm² = 1.47

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2-modified Pt shows sharp OH bridging peaks 3600-3800 cm⁻¹ assigned to OHad on Ce atoms of various valence, absent in ionomer-coated Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the wavenumber range from 3600 to 3800 cm⁻¹, sharp peaks are distinctly observed only in the spectrum of the CeO2-modified Pt/Si prism.
